rationale.NCEI-native-duration: Select curved mean with existing distance-varying residual SD and event effect; keep linear mean with same residual/event forms as runner-up. The accepted sequence CV point gain is 0.08389189150672258nats/record; descriptive clustered95% interval [-0.04872626774297359,0.21651005075641874] includes 0. Native near-field predictions differ materially and curve improves some held-out discrepancies, so the amended plan permits a working curved choice with an uncertain gain. Base gamma 0.545[0.420,0.676] remains 0.613[0.479,0.741] after jointly deleting Tohoku/Chile and0.552[0.426,0.679] with gamma prior widened. These are marginal posterior summaries, not predictive-score comparisons or physical curvature proof. Both forms retain substantial in-sample PPC misses; unresolved36 cannot favor curve. Era/subset differences require explicit scope limitations. Curvature is not stable across all era-only cohorts: gamma is 0.919 [0.680,1.144] before 2007, 0.461 [0.276,0.646] in 2007–2013, and -0.111 [-0.450,0.239] in 2014 onward (90% marginal posterior intervals). Those data-selected contrasts do not identify era causes or establish universal curvature; unresolved linear36 prevents the recent-era comparison of linear and curved mean forms.

Distance form is runner-up because its lower equal-event mean absolute error (43.088 versus 69.376 minutes, distance versus pooled) is a real scientific tradeoff, while its primary score difference vs pooled is -0.33226476137225364 with descriptive clustered95% interval [-1.1408288076424031,0.4762992848978959]. No equivalence or universal winner claimed; this choice does not discard distance-dependent predictions.
